sheet-47.description: The lower half of sheet 47 shows the northwest corner of Bay Head in Section B, west of Twilight Lake, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The upper half of the page carries the title block and the key map of the whole town, which are not part of this georeferenced area; the Sanborn legend box at the top right of the map area is cut out of the mask as well. The part covers three rows of platted blocks between West Avenue on the west and West Lake Avenue on the east, crossed by Bay Avenue in the middle. Cranberry Avenue and Woodland Avenue run across the sheet, and an alley runs along the bottom edge, where the plan continues on sheet 49. The northern edge of the plat is a long diagonal line closing the top row of lots, and a dashed line along the west side marks the edge of the platted land beyond West Avenue. Every block is divided into narrow numbered lots, most about 25 to 50 feet wide, with lot numbers and block numbers 1 to 6 printed in the blocks. No buildings at all are drawn on this part: in 1905 this was an undeveloped subdivision of paper lots awaiting sale. The street widths are lettered at the block corners, mostly 50 feet, with 40 feet for some cross streets. East of West Lake Avenue the sheet shows the western shore of Twilight Lake, and at the bottom right South Lake Avenue begins to curve along the lake shore toward sheet 50. A compass rose stands at the left edge, and the scale bar reads sixty feet to one inch.
notes: Bay Av. is today's Holly Avenue and West Av. is today's Western Avenue (OpenStreetMap); the spacing of the junctions matches.
No buildings are drawn: an unbuilt subdivision in 1905.
The key map and title block in the upper half of the page are left out of the mask.
Population note in the title block: winter 300, summer 2000; no water facilities for fire service, no fire department.

map, 60 ft. Upper half is title block and key map of the town (left out of the mask); lower half is one part: Cranberry Av, Woodland Av, West Av (Western Avenue), Bay Av (Holly Avenue), W. Lake Av. Unbuilt subdivision. Legend box notched out.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers the northern end of Bay Head's oceanfront district, Section A, between Twilight Lake on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Three streets run the length of the sheet: East Lake Avenue along the lake shore, Main Avenue in the middle and East Avenue toward the beach. They are crossed, from north to south, by Division Street at the top edge, North Street, Karge Street and Harris Street at the bottom, where the plan continues on sheet 51. The blocks are cut into deep numbered lots. Development is thin at the north end and denser toward Harris Street. The main buildings are large summer hotels: The Ocean View, between East Lake and Main avenues just south of North Street, and The Grenville with its outbuildings and The Grenville Arms, a large hotel with an open porch, between Main and East avenues near Harris Street. Elsewhere the sheet shows scattered frame dwellings with porches, a few stables and many vacant lots. A boardwalk, drawn as a dashed double line with yellow hatching, runs south from Karge Street behind the oceanfront lots east of East Avenue. Above Division Street, beyond the town line, the sheet marks the adjoining area as not covered. Street widths of 40 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners. A compass rose stands near the beach at the upper right, with the sheet number and the scale bar beside it.
notes: Main Av. is today's Ocean Avenue, E. Lake Av. is today's Lake Avenue; North, Karge and Harris are North Street, Karge Street and Harris Street.
Division (the top street) matches today's Twilight Road in position.
Hotels: The Ocean View, The Grenville, The Grenville Arms.
map, 60 ft. Division (Twilight Road), North, Karge, Harris x E. Lake Av (Lake Avenue), Main Av (Ocean Avenue), East Av. One part.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 shows the western part of Bay Head in Section B, west of Twilight Lake, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Bay Avenue and West Lake Avenue run down the sheet, with West Avenue along the western edge drawn on a slanting line, and they are crossed from north to south by Park Avenue, Bridge Avenue, Grove Avenue and Meadow Avenue. At the top right corner South Lake Avenue runs off diagonally along the lake toward sheet 50. The blocks between West and West Lake avenues are regular, each divided into sixteen narrow numbered lots with block numbers 5 to 17. Development is sparse: a few frame dwellings and sheds stand on Park Avenue near West Lake Avenue and at the corner of Grove and West Lake avenues, and a scatter of small houses and outbuildings lies on unplatted land west of West Avenue. A small frame public school stands on the north side of Meadow Avenue east of Bay Avenue, and next to it a small green-coloured shop building whose label begins with a blacksmith abbreviation. The rest of the blocks are vacant lots. Street widths are lettered at the corners, 70 feet for Bridge Avenue and 40 to 50 feet for the others. Below Meadow Avenue the plan is continued only as block outlines for the area not covered by the atlas. A compass rose is drawn at the upper right and the scale bar at the lower left reads sixty feet to one inch.
notes: Bay Av. is today's Holly Avenue; West Av. is today's Western Avenue, which today ends at Woodland Avenue; Grove Av. is today's Grove Street.
Public school on Meadow Avenue.
map, 60 ft. Park, Bridge, Grove (Grove Street), Meadow x West Av (Western Avenue), Bay Av (Holly Avenue), W. Lake Av. Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers the centre of Bay Head around the railroad terminus, between West Lake Avenue on the west and East Lake Avenue on the east, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Twilight Lake fills the top of the sheet and drains south through a narrow channel crossed by bridges at Bridge Avenue and Howe Street. South Lake Avenue runs diagonally along the lake shore at the top left. Park, Bridge, Grove and Meadow avenues cross West Lake Avenue and Railroad Avenue on the west side; Howe Street and Mount Street meet East Lake Avenue on the east side, and Harris Street is noted at the top right. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs down the middle of the sheet on its own right of way, with a depot, a freight house and an ice house beside the tracks. The commercial centre is on Bridge Avenue: a grocery, stores and a bakery at the lake shore, the Bay Head House hotel, and the Z. P. Van Note livery. Hall's livery stands on Grove Avenue and there are carpenter shops on Grove Avenue and East Lake Avenue. Institutions include the M. E. Church on Park Avenue, the Presbyterian church, the borough hall and post office with a lock-up and tool house on East Lake Avenue, and the Episcopal church near Howe Street. Dwellings with stables fill much of the west side. The sheet is split between Section A east of the channel and Section B west of it.
notes: Railroad Av. (west of the tracks) matches today's Club Drive in position; its junctions fit 1.8 to 3.5 m off, against under 2 m for the other streets.
E. Lake Av. is today's Lake Avenue; Grove Av. is Grove Street; Howe and Mount are Howe Street and Mount Street.
Pennsylvania Railroad depot, freight house and ice house; bridges over the Twilight Lake outlet at Bridge Avenue and Howe Street.
Borough hall and post office, M. E. Church, Presbyterian church and Episcopal church on this sheet.
map, 60 ft. Centre: W. Lake Av, Railroad Av (Club Drive), Pennsylvania RR, E. Lake Av (Lake Avenue); Park, Bridge, Grove, Meadow, Howe, Mount. One part.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 covers the middle of Bay Head's oceanfront district, Section A, between Twilight Lake on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. East Lake Avenue, Main Avenue and East Avenue run down the sheet and are crossed by Harris Street at the top, Bridge Avenue, Howe Street and Mount Street at the bottom, where the plan continues on sheet 52. West of East Lake Avenue the sheet shows only the edge of the lake and the blocks drawn in full on sheet 50. This is the most built-up residential part of the town, with frame cottages of two to three stories, many with open porches, on most lots, and stables behind several of them. The largest building is the hotel The Bellevue in the block between Harris Street and Bridge Avenue, west of Main Avenue, and Smith Ho. stands on Main Avenue south of Bridge Avenue. On East Lake Avenue near Mount Street the town's water works are drawn: a 20,000 gallon water tank on an iron tower, marked for domestic supply only, with a small pump building, an office and a carpenter shop. East of East Avenue the oceanfront lots back onto a boardwalk drawn as a dashed double line, with a row of small bath houses behind one lot. Street widths of 40 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners. A compass rose stands on the lake shore at the left, with a foot bridge at the lower left corner and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Main Av. is today's Ocean Avenue and E. Lake Av. is today's Lake Avenue.
Water tower: 20,000 gallon tank on an iron tower, domestic supply only.
Hotel The Bellevue; Smith Ho.
map, 60 ft. Harris, Bridge, Howe, Mount x E. Lake Av, Main Av (Ocean Avenue), East Av. One part.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the southern end of Bay Head between Barnegat Bay on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Mount Street crosses the top of the sheet; below it Main Avenue and East Avenue run down the sheet, and two streets lettered only as Street cross the lower half, laid out but still unbuilt. East Lake Avenue is drawn only as a short stub at the top left and is not labelled here. The large block 1A west of Main Avenue runs to the bay shore, with a foot bridge at its northern end; it is almost empty apart from a group of stores and a grocery on Mount Street, a wood shed and a few scattered dwellings and outbuildings. Between Main and East avenues stand the U.S. Life Saving Station, several dwellings and a bath house building. East of East Avenue the oceanfront holds the large hotel The Bluffs with its annex and a row of large cottages, all backing onto a boardwalk drawn as a dashed double line with yellow hatching that ends south of block 3A. The southern half of the sheet, blocks 4A and 5A, is drawn only as outlines of undivided land with no buildings. Street widths of 40 to 70 feet are lettered at the corners. A compass rose stands on the bay shore at the left and the scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Main Av. is today's Ocean Avenue. The two cross streets lettered only 'Street' do not match any modern street in position (Forsythe and Chadwick streets lie about 150 and 180 m south of Mount Street; the first drawn street is about 290 m south).
U.S. Life Saving Station; hotel The Bluffs with annex.
Placed from the three junctions on Mount Street only (one detected, two hand-picked): low confidence toward the south end.
